Introduction

Audience, Scope, and Purpose

 

The Cerence Cloud Services (CCS) platform is Cerence’s multi-tenant, cloud-based speech recognition and infotainment solution. The CCS platform transforms connected vehicles into natural user experiences by leveraging Cerence’s voice recognition, natural language understanding, predictive text, and content capabilities. CCS is capable of processing large volumes of transactions to deliver requested services.

 

This document is for Cerence automotive customers who plan to deploy and use Cerence Cloud Services in and through Cerence designated third-party, cloud service providers.

This document provides an overview of the CCS solution with a focus on Data Strategy within the solution. Data Strategy provides a comprehensive view of the data that is collected, the data that is generated, how the data is stored, and the privacy/security mechanisms surrounding the data processing. Cerence’s goal with this whitepaper is to transparently provide a holistic view of data flow, so that our customers can implement their data privacy policy and comply with privacy regulations such as the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

 

 

Document Status

 

This document has been reviewed by Cerence Engineering and Product Management. It describes the Cerence Cloud architecture and practices related to data privacy and security on the date of publication. Updates to the document will be published to reflect changes in the Cerence Cloud Services (CCS) solution, which are driven by new features, technology innovations, legislative changes, and other factors.

 

CCS Solution Overview

CCS Data Flow Overview

 

The CCS platform receives end-user requests from Vehicle Head Units directly or through a Customer Gateway. The request is processed within the Cerence Runtime Environment (in some cases while interacting with Third Party Content Providers to retrieve infotainment content), and a response is returned to the Vehicle Head Unit.

 

System health information is delivered to the Cerence Global Operations Center (GOC) to ensure service quality and availability objectives. Usage metrics are delivered to the Cerence Business Intelligence System to support service management and accounting functions. Some meta data generated during processing is delivered to the Cerence Research Grid for offline analysis and continuous improvement of the core technology.

 

When a driver invokes a speech-enabled application on the Vehicle Head Unit, the local, embedded application will collect a spoken command (e.g., "How's the weather in Atlanta on Saturday?") and stream that input through the customer Gateway to the CCS Runtime Environment.  The results of the voice command will be returned to the vehicle where local arbitration logic in the Cerence’s embedded software will determine whether the final result to the driver should be derived from the embedded voice synthesis software or from the voice synthesis software located on the CCS platform.  

 

 

Vehicle/Gateway Overview

 

The Vehicle Head Unit creates the user interface to applications running within and outside the vehicle. Upon activation by the driver, customer applications collect input from audio and other sensors for processing and rendering responses in the car’s cockpit. These voice command requests are sent via secure TLS link through the customer Gateway to the CCS platform for real-time processing.

 

One key function of the customer applications running on the Vehicle Head Unit is that they create and pass a Globally Unique ID (GUID) when connecting to the customer Gateway to pass speech processing requests. Creating the GUID is entirely within the customer’s control, and the GUID should be unique for each vehicle. Cerence understands that the GUID can be disassociated from the driver. It should not be a vehicle identification number, telephone number, or any other form of personal data. From the perspective of CCS, this customer created GUID is an “external ID”.

 

A second key function of the customer applications running on the Vehicle Head Unit is the ability to upload text data (Language Model Enrollment, “LME”, data) to improve speech recognition performance. It is envisioned that the customer applications may upload contact names from a local address book. These names are used to statistically bias recognition results in real-time and therefore improve recognition performance.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

CCS Solution Component Overview

 

CCS Runtime Environment: The CCS Runtime Environment processes real-time end-user requests. It is designed for performance, scalability, and availability. The CCS Runtime Environment contains the Cerence Service Gateway, Cerence Processing Engines, and Cerence Operating Tools.

Cerence Service Gateway: Within the CCS Runtime Environment, the Cerence Service Gateway manages incoming end-user requests and sessions. One key function of the Cerence Service Gateway is to transform “external IDs” created by customer applications on the Vehicle Head-Unit (and other customer applications) to an “internal ID”. This transformation from external ID to internal ID is accomplished through an irreversible one-way cryptographic hash function completed at the very start of a session within the gateway. Hashing the external ID into an internal ID ensures that any processing of an end-user’s request is further disassociated from the user and any data created by that processing does not contain the external ID.

 

Cerence Processing Engines: Within the CCS Runtime Environment, the Cerence Processing Engines apply numerous transformations and algorithms using large statistical models to take the driver’s spoken command, transforming it into a text translation and deciphering its intent. If provided by the customer applications, LME data is used to bias real-time recognition results. As a result of this processing, the Processing Engines create speech data logs which contain spoken utterance and processing performance information. Upon mutual agreement, LME data will not be logged.

 

Cerence Operations Tools: Within the CCS Runtime Environment, the Cerence Operations Tools receive infrastructure logs (e.g. syslogs) from servers, network devices, etc. These logs do not contain voice utterance data or other application-layer data resulting from the processing of end-user requests.

Cerence Global Operations Center: The Cerence Global Operations Center (GOC) monitors the CCS Runtime Environment 24x7, 365 days per-year. Performance indicators, metrics and system health information from the CCS Runtime Environment are presented to GOC engineers to ensure high performance and availability levels. These performance indicators, metrics, and system health information do not contain voice utterance data or other application-layer data resulting from the processing of end-user requests.

 

Cerence Business Intelligence System: The Cerence Business Intelligence System receives usage metrics from the CCS Runtime Environment to support service management and accounting functions. These data do not contain voice utterance. The output of BI are aggregate results containing project-layer metrics from the processing of all end-user requests. Examples of this aggregate results include the number of transactions and command type breakdown. The aggregate results are generated for each RTE data center).

Third Party Content Providers: CCS interacts with Third-Party Content Providers (e.g., Vaisala, HERE, etc.) to retrieve infotainment content for some end-user requests. Queries to these Third Party Content Providers do not contain voice utterance data and only contain current geo-location and minimum-required information from end-user requests to fulfill the request. For example, if a driver asked, ‘How's the weather in Atlanta on Saturday?’, the query to the weather Content Provider would contain the geo-location for the current location of the vehicle, the city of Atlanta, and Saturday as the day, each as query parameters.) Queries to Third Party Content Providers do not contain user IDs of any sort, and queries are performed over an encrypted channel (e.g., HTTPS) to/from the provider.

 

Cerence Research Grid (CRG): The Cerence Research Grid receives speech data logs from the CCS Runtime Environment. These data are created by the Processing Engines and consist of logs which contain the internal ID, spoken utterance, resulting transcription, interpretation, and processing performance information. The speech data logs are stored on the Cerence Research Grid at a user-level, but do not retain any other directly identifying information about that user.

 

 

CCS Logging Overview

 

The CCS cloud components log data to a central component the RTE called CLI or Cloud Logging Infrastructure which merges all information into unified log files for each voice command request (transaction). These logs are transferred to the Cerence Research Grid, and a portion of these logs (for example, no voice utterances) are transferred to the BI platform.

A data obfuscation process resides within the CLI as part of the log merge process. The following data privacy related functions are applied:

 

·                      Geolocations are coarsened to only one decimal place (by default), or suppressed completely from logs.

·                      Recognition and Interpretation results are filtered per domain

o       For example, SMS message composition transactions have the audio in the logs completely removed and any recognition and interpretation results suppressed

 

Some filtering/suppression rules are applied globally, and some are applied on an application specific or data center specific basis. These rules are controlled through log filtering/suppression configuration files maintained in each Cerence data centers. When third party or local results are determined and before being returned to the vehicle to complete processing, these results will also be included in the speech data log. Customers may reach out to Cerence to request more restrictive filtering and log suppression rules be applied. These are the only logs available for troubleshooting, for research, and for business intelligence.

 

End User consenting to Cerence Cloud Services (CCS):   The customer is responsible for collecting the consent from and/or providing the appropriate notice to their end users to enable Cerence cloud services. If the consent is not completed or the end user withdraws his/her consent, then Cerence Cloud Services can be disabled for a particular vehicle. When CCS is disabled, all voice assistant services will remain in the vehicle, handled by Cerence’s embedded software only. No embedded speech logs will be sent to CCS when it is disabled.

Opt-out/Opt-in: Cerence APIs allow an application to configure a transaction as “opt-in” or “opt-out” of logging. It is the responsibility of the in-car application to collect that information (ex. via GUI) and pass that in the CCS transaction.

Transactions carrying the “opt-out” flag will have all information in the log suppressed, except for a few critical fields such as application ID, time stamps and server utilization timings. If CCS is disabled, the configuration of logging is moot since no data is collected by CCS.

 

End User consenting to Product Improvements: In addition, the embedded software provides the upstream software the capability to set a product improvement flag to FALSE as a mechanism to opt out of product improvements. Setting this flag FALSE at the user-level will disable speech data logs from flowing to the CRG, preventing future voice data collected from this user from being used to build or train our next-generation voice models.  So, for example, if the GUI developer offers a specific, separate consent for product improvements and the end user declines to consent or withdraws this consent, the developer should set this flag to FALSE to complete the opt out mechanism.

 

CCS Deployment Architecture

 

Runtime Environments

 

Cerence currently has CCS runtime environments in different regions to handle the requests from customer head-units globally. In each region, CCS runtime environment is deployed in a public cloud environment. The runtime environments are:

·                      North America

o       CCS runtime is deployed in public cloud based in Virginia, USA2.

o       NA Runtime environments are provisioned to handle customer traffic from the Americas, Asia (non-China), Oceania (including Australia and New Zealand) when the user sets VR language to US-English, AU-English, or SGP-English.

 

·                      Europe

o       CCS runtime is deployed in public cloud based in Amsterdam, Netherlands2.

o       Europe Runtime environments are provisioned to handle customer traffic from Europe, Africa, and the Middle East.

o       Anywhere else when the user selects an EU-based language.

 

·                      China

o       CCS runtime is deployed in public cloud based in Zhangjiakou and Shanghai, China2.

o       China Runtime environments is provisioned to handle all customer traffic originating from mainland China.

 

·                      Japan

o       CCS runtime is deployed in public cloud based in Saitama, Japan2.

o       Japan Runtime environment is provisioned to handle customer traffic from Asia outside of mainland China, including Macao and Hong Kong.

o       Anywhere else when user sets VR language to Chinese Mandarin or Cantonese.

2 NOTE: Cerence may add to or change these locations as part of capacity planning and optimization process. Cerence will inform customers (that launch) of any such planned changes.

 

 

Cerence GOC

 

The role of the Cerence Global Operations Center (GOC) is to provide 24 x 7 support for Cerence’s worldwide cloud hosted services and operations.

 

·                      The GOC is in Marlow, UK and Pune India

·                      The Marlow GOC operates 7am to 7pm UK UTC

·                      The Pune GOC operates 7pm to 7am UK UTC

 

 

Cerence Research Grid

 

Data in the Cerence Research Grid (CRG) is disaggregated from its runtime form when data is moved from the Cerence Runtime Environment. The CRG maintained this speech data as one large monolithic structure. 

At the direction of the customer, voice call logs can be disabled from being transferred to the CRG or speech data logs can be anonymized by zeroizing the internal UID field.

For most current deployments, the disassociated audio files, otherwise known as ‘utterances’, are normally a few seconds in length, which further contributes to the anonymity. Similarly, the utterances are normally simple directive commands that do not contain personal data. By disaggregating the data, sufficiently large data pools are created. Furthermore, Cerence has conducted its own research and concluded that where all the features described above are deployed, it is virtually impossible to identify a known data subject from voice alone.

 

Cerence Research Grid receives speech data logs from the CCS Runtime Environment which is then used for various improvements by Cerence researchers. Cerence Research GRID processes logs globally as follows:

·                      North America

o       The North America Grid is based out of a Cerence-managed data center located in Somerville, MA, USA. Backups are stored in an Azure US East 2 data center in Virginia.

·                      Europe

o       Currently, there is no research grid in Europe. All runtime logs are stored in the European runtime environment before being sent to the North American grid location.

·                      China

o       Currently, there is no research grid in China. All runtime logs are stored in the China runtime environment to comply with local regulations. The logs are anonymized before being sent to the North American grid location.

·                      Japan

o       Currently, there is no research grid in Japan. All runtime logs are stored in the Japan runtime environment before being sent to the North American grid location.

 

 

Cerence Business Intelligence System

 

The Cerence Business Intelligence System receives application log data from the CCS Runtime Environment to support service management and accounting functions. This data does not contain voice utterances and only contains application- layer metrics resulting from the processing of end-user requests (e.g., number of customer transactions in EU data centers).

 

Business Intelligence systems are currently hosted in Azure US East 2.

 

Detailed Node Architecture

CCS Runtime Environment

 

Access Control

 

Cerence Runtime Environments are accessible by the Cerence hosted operations Site Reliability Engineering teams and Engineering DevOps teams. Cerence Runtime Environment is fully protected via VPN-based connections and policy-based access controls integrated with Cerence Active Directory. Groups and permissions are put in place to make sure that only authorized people have access to this environment.

Call Log Processing:

Call Log storage system that is part of the CCS runtime environment, merges the call logs from multiple CCS components. Each time a component is processing part of a global transaction, a call log piece is created and sent to Call Log storage system (immediately after the transaction is completed). Periodically, the Call Log storage system reassembles the call log pieces to form a merged call log. During the merging process, call logs are modified to comply with customer security policies (e.g. do not store audio, do not store ASR/NLU results for messaging domain). When a call log has been merged, it becomes available for processing by the GRID backend and BI system. Each system will separately pull the parts of the merged logs they are allowed to on a regular interval.

 

Business Intelligence (BI)

 

The Cerence Business Intelligence System receives application log data from the CCS Runtime Environment to support service management and accounting functions. These data do not contain voice utterance data and only contain application-layer metrics resulting from the processing of end-user requests (e.g. number of customer transactions in EU data centers). The only personal data sent to the BI are the ASR results (to track top 10 usage statistics for customer reports), the Internal ID (to track unique user and overall traffic usage) and NLU domain (to track type of usage for customer reports)

 

All Runtime Environments integrate with the same central BI system in the Azure US East 2 Region. Business Intelligence System is hosted in the Azure US East 2 Region. Data is sent to the BI system for the following purposes:

 

·                      Driving reporting for customers, which can be used for monitoring, analyses, SLA adherence, billing, understanding usage and customer segmentation, propensity etc.

·                      Generated reports can be used by Cerence for billing, product improvement, monitoring latency/SLA/capacity analysis, forecasting etc.

·                      Summarized Data stored for longer periods can be used for machine-learning/AI activities to gain more insight and deliver better experiences to end users.

 

BI Data Flow

 

Data from the various runtime environments (e.g. US, Europe etc..) is extracted from the CLI and transformed into a model appropriate for summarization and reporting, and then transferred to a central data warehouse in Azure’s US East region, then loaded into OLAP data cubes. Reporting and analytics are then driven out of these OLAP cubes and optionally accessed through a secure (SSL) web portal.

 

Access Control

 

There are three types of access to the BI system:

 

1.                      External Customers (i.e. customers) via the BI Portal (Optional)

 

The BI portal is configured to allow customers to see only aggregate reports specific to their deployment. Each user (CCS customer) must be provisioned and configured explicitly before accessing the BI portal and accessing the reports.

 

2.                      Internal (Cerence) customers via the BI Portal or Portal reports

 

The BI portal is also configured to allow internal Cerence users to generate aggregate ONLY reports to garner insights and other purposes listed above. The aggregate reports can be produced specific to a customer / customer project or across customers / customer projects.

 

3.                      Developers / Administrators

 

Developers and Administrators are Cerence employees / contractors who need access to the BI systems for developing and maintaining it. These employees/ contractors are provisioned with specific permissions before they can access the BI system. Access to the BI systems is on a need-to-know basis only

 

 

Global Operations Center (GOC)

 

The role of the GOC is to provide 24 x 7 support for Cerence’s worldwide hosted services and operations. To that end it is staffed 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year, with highly trained personnel charged with insuring service uptimes and compliance with established service level agreements. All Incident Managers responsible to run Cerence’s Event, Incident, Problem and Change Management processes, are ITIL v3 Foundation certified. All GOC Engineers are RHCSA/RHCE trained to provide first and second line support for Cerence’s products and services.

 

The GOC performs proactive monitoring of Cerence’s hosted infrastructure, networks and applications and is the primary customer contact center for reporting issues and events. Events result in the creation of GOC tickets to record event impacts, start times and resolution times as well as all associated incident responses and actions to restore service. They perform various tasks including coordinating incident response bridges for service impacting incidents/events/alerts, notifying customers of event status, and coordinating Tier 1 and Tier 2 responses through to complete issue resolution. The GOC tracks performance KPIs and reports on service performance regularly. They drive the internal problem management process to eliminate recurring, service impacting incidents and drive continuous improvement in service quality and uptime. The GOC also coordinates all changes necessary to perform upgrades and maintenance of Cerence's hosted infrastructure and services, ensuring alignment with designated maintenance intervals, and is the central point of coordination for any security-related incidents detected by the Security Incident and Event Management (SIEM) process. The GOC also controls user access to Cerence’s hosted networks and infrastructure, granting least privilege access as necessary and in compliance with Cerence's Global Security Policies.

 

The GOC staff are currently located in Marlow, UK and Pune, India. They have access and are able to monitor and intervene to fix service impacting issues in all regions. The GOC staff also has access to additional second- and third-line support engineers through an On-Call pager rotation should more in-depth troubleshooting be required to resolve an issue. On-Call staff are located throughout the world in Europe, Americas, and Asia.

 

GOC locations are connected to Cerence’s worldwide networks with Dual ISP network connections ensuring connectivity necessary to maintain services and operations.

Data Consumed by the GOC contains no personal data. There are several classes of data that flow to the GOC to monitor and maintain operations. These include Infrastructure Logs, Metrics Data, Synthetic Transaction Data, and Monitoring Data. There is no personal data allowed in any of these datasets.

·                      Infrastructure Logs are comprised of systems logs, container logs, and application logs. These logs provide information related to the physical and virtual assets that host the application.

·                      Metrics Data is comprised of network data (send/receive, error rates), Disk data (usage, read/write speeds,

errors, latency), CPU data (usage), Memory Data (usage).

·                      Synthetic Transaction Data emulates a client transaction with test inputs to verify successful transaction processing.

·                      Monitoring Data is aggregated and correlated from the log, metrics and synthetic transaction data and expressed to the GOC in the form of Alerts or Events and Dashboards showing metrics.

 

The GOC has access to aggregated BI information (which is non-personal), but has no access to data on the Cerence Research Grid.

 


Data Usage, Access and Retention

Data Usage

 

Cerence Runtime Environment / Global Operations Center

 

Data in the runtime environments allows Cerence engineers to diagnose system issues based on customer reporting as well as for periodic internal analysis.

 

 

Cerence Business Intelligence System

 

Data in Business Intelligence system is used for:

 

·                      Driving the reporting for customers (customers) which can be used for monitoring, analyses, SLA adherence, billing, understanding usage and customer segmentation, propensity etc.

·                      Generating reports that can be used by Cerence for billing, product improvement, monitoring latency/SLA/capacity analysis, forecasting etc.

·                      Gaining deeper insight and delivering better experiences to end users, by leveraging data stored over longer periods for machine-learning/AI modeling.

Cerence Research Grid

 

Cerence Research Grid: The Cerence Research Grid receives speech data logs from the CCS Runtime Environment. These data are created by the Processing Engines and consist of logs which contain a pseudonymized, internal ID, a spoken utterance, a resulting text transcription of the audio, an interpretation (intention) of the user request, and some processing performance information. This speech data log is considered “disassociated data” since is stored on the Cerence Research Grid in that we know the data is only from a single user, but do not know any directly identifying information about that user.

 

Acoustic / Language / NLU Model Updates: An acoustic model encodes how sounds are represented in words, such as what the ‘a’ in “cat” sounds like. A language model encodes how words combine into phrases that have meaning. Using these two types of models, as well as dictionaries and other input, voice recognition software will output the most likely sequence of what was said.

Within the Cerence Research Grid raw speech data is aggregated and used to build the statistical acoustic, language and NLU models that power the Cerence Processing Engines in the Runtime Environment. Such models are trained on hundreds to thousands of hours of speech, and millions to billions of words of text data (transcribed audio from real users saying real things).

 

Speaker-Independent Language Model Adaptation: Within the Cerence Research Grid, the Speaker- Independent Language Model Adaptation (SI-LMA) process improves recognition of market-specific and new trending terms. It is also used to fix some bugs or misrecognitions.

 

Speaker-Dependent Acoustic Model Adaptation: Within the Cerence Research Grid, audio from end-user utterances are used to build acoustic model adaptations that optimize the statistics and recognition for users who

use the system frequently. This optimization process is called Speaker-Dependent Acoustic Model Adaptation (SD- AMA).

Cerence uses deep learning technology for statistical acoustic, language and NLU modeling. The technology is data driven and can produce better model from using more data. Pooling data from all customers together in our research and factory model training process can achieve better accuracy than using customer data for customer specific models.

All users will get additional accuracy improvement from speaker-dependent adaptation using their own data. In addition, each application tends to have differences in how user intents are expressed (e.g. due to screen tutorials, commercials, manuals, demographics of owners, familiarity with previous voice systems) and have different acoustic condition distributions. Improvement from using customer data for customer specific application scenario via speaker-independent adaptation and modeling is also unique for customers’ drivers.

 

 

Data Access

 

Data stored in the Cerence Research Grid is protected by group permissions administered at the corporate level. Access to that data is permitted only on an as-needed basis on a least privilege model. That is, only those researchers who must use specific data to create or improve relevant products are permitted to access that data. Such access is granted only upon manager request, after verifying the researcher is up-to-date on all required data privacy and security training. Once granted, access is only obtained by approved individuals through secondary authentication. Access is either renewed or revoked whenever a researcher’s job changes, and is generally reviewed on a bi-yearly basis Data privacy and security courses must be taken yearly..

 

The Cerence Research Group has language specific linguist experts as well as language-independent more general system experts and deep learning experts. They work together to deliver the best possible solutions and services to our customer customers.

As a global organization and market leader, we recruit the best system and deep learning experts around the globe, and these are not all concentrated in one location. Collaborative effort involving all these experts speeds up troubleshooting and enhances our ability to meet SLA requirements.

 

 

Cerence Data Retention

 

Cerence Runtime Environment / Global Operations Center

 

Speech data logs within the Cerence Runtime Environment are maintained for up to 28 days to support debugging and troubleshooting activities. These speech data logs are sent to the Research Grid to support acoustic, language, and NLU modeling activities and do contain voice utterance data resulting from the processing of end-user requests.

 

Language Model Enrollment (“LME”) data provided by the customer applications and maintained in the Cerence Runtime Environment is purged upon 6 months of user inactivity.

Infrastructure logs within the Cerence Runtime Environment are maintained for 90 days or longer as required for audit purposes. These logs do not contain voice utterance data or other application-layer data resulting from the processing of end-user requests.

 

 

Cerence Business Intelligence System

 

The Usage data sent from the CCS Runtime Environment to the Cerence Business Intelligence System is maintained for 6-7 months to ensure two quarters worth of aggregate reports can be produced on-the-fly. Aggregate data reports produced by the Business Intelligence systems are retained for 13 months but are also backed-up / archived for 2 additional years.

 

 

Cerence Research Grid

 

Cerence has also deployed the 3-year retention on a rolling basis and this data retention standard further protects the data by removing data at the end of its useful life cycle. Cerence maintains policies, controls, and customer commitments not to “re-associate” disassociated audio data, even if future technology allows it. Cerence is mindful of its obligations as a data processor and ensures that it does not make any use of the data other than for the purposes for which is was collected.

 

End-user data (audio and logs) on the CRG is managed by a centralized Data Team, in a collection of directories and file systems called the “vault”. Vault data is typically stored in large .zip files and indexes of these zip files are held in databases. Backups of the vault files are done by the Data Team. The .zip files are archived as objects in containers. It is prohibited for researcher to make copies of audio and/or logs from vault files, so data sets are generally just collections of pointers to data in the vault. This allows the Data Team to honor requests for deleting the data of individual users (identified via the “internal ID”) and/or of individual applications. The deletions take effect on the vault and backups of the vault files.

 

In some cases, data from many users is combined with no link to any specific speaker utterance. Since even the “internal ID” associated with that data is dropped, the aggregated data becomes even more fully anonymized. It may consist of:

 

•                      Feature vectors derived from the audio files.

•                      Text combined from many users after identifying information (such as phone numbers) is obfuscated.

•                      Annotated intents common to multiple users.

 

Retaining the aggregated data allows Cerence to create and support voice models. For acoustic model training, the original speech data in the “vault” may still be needed, but no copies are made, and access is always done through the vault. User data on the CRG is only accessed from the Research Grid via terminal, remote desktop, or browser access from the researcher’s laptop / workstation. The connections to the CRG are always made within Cerence’s VPN. Copies of the data to a researcher’s laptop / workstation are restricted.

 

 

Reduced Data Retention Period Impacts

 

Both our deep learning factory model training, adaptation process, and speaker-dependent adaptation process can make effective use of 3 years of data. Reducing retention period less than 3 years limits the accuracy improvement potential from exploring field data. Since training data from a given application disproportionately improves performance for that application as compared to others, factory models may be specifically less optimal for customer applications.

 

In addition, there will be much less amount of speaker-dependent data for adaptation for customer drivers. It is even possible that some drivers may see performance degradation if they don’t use the system for an extended period. Finally, there is a non-trivial processing time and cost to transcribe and annotate data before it can be available for researchers for experimentation and help baseline performance over time. A longer retention period of 12 years is maintained to sustain this data. This special data set makes up a fraction (less than 1%) of all customer data collected.  

Data Privacy Management

Privacy Management

 

Cerence has established a privacy program managed by the Data Owner(s) and the Legal Department, supported by a matrix structure within its business units. Cerence strives for openness and transparency with customers about how data is used and secured. To that end, Cerence has established an online privacy policy and has implemented a maximum retention period of 3 years for even pseudonymized personal data. Cerence has also implemented administrative data protection and security measures, such as policies and procedures regarding standard data access and use practices by employees, physical access controls, secondary authentication and access requirements, audit trails, logging, and monitoring. Global employee training, covering information protection and data security, is provided annually, and is supplemented by additional ad hoc training and communications as needed.

 

 

Requests for Information

 

If Cerence receives requests from third parties for user information. Cerence may release information regarding users if:

 

1.                      A customer directs Cerence to do so OR

2.                      If it is required as part of a legal or judicial process, in response to a subpoena or court order, a statutory requirement or exemption, in an emergency to prevent a crime or protect national security.

Cerence does not provide direct access to any government agency to customer or end user data. If compelled to disclose customer or end user data under applicable legal process, Cerence will notify the customer unless legally prohibited from doing so.
